title: The Lincoln Theatre with Ellington's Washingtonians, and Fats Waller
summary: Stranded in New York, she played the Lincoln Theatre in Harlem with Seymour and Jeanette alongside Duke Ellington's Washingtonians and met Fats Waller, who made audiences scream.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Yep. We got stranded in New York and so we went back to Pittsburgh, Joe Williams, John, and I, then later on to Memphis with John. During this period is when I met Fats Waller.
When you were in New York with Seymour and Jeanette?

Yes. We had a date in the Lincoln Theatre - I imagine you've heard of the Lincoln Theatre in Harlem? Duke Ellington had just come into New York with his combo, the Washingtonians they were. They were playing the Lincoln with us because Seymour and Jeanette were the top black act. So he played on stage with the band and they had me in the pit playing with the band. Still couldn't read. I played in the band with Tricky Sam, Bubber Miley, and Sonny Greer, and then I'd go up on stage with the act. I met Fats Waller then and I can tell you he was just a sensation in New York, when they'd turn the light on people would scream, when he sat down, people would scream. I never saw such a thing. When he finished, that was the end; they had to let it cool off.
Was he playing the organ just as a solo specialty?
No.... He probably was playing for the movie but this week he did a tune before the show.
I remember someone telling me he used to play for the news reel. Nobody was watching the news reel and he did all kind of things.
